configureKeypadConnectorWarning: When reconnecting the keypad, align the plug with the entire row of pins. Check that every pin is seated in its corresponding opening and that none remain outside the plug.
valveBoardAlt: Lower edge of the Autolejek board with relay connector 1 and its GND and VOUT terminals highlighted.
configureDetectorGland: Feed the detector cable through the fourth gland from the left, at the far right when facing the gland panel from outside the enclosure.
configureDetectorGlandAlt: Outside view of the enclosure with gland 4 highlighted.
configureDetectorTrim: Trim the excess with side cutters. Leave about 10 cm of cable inside, measured from the inside edge next to the gland. Check that the conductors reach the terminals without tension. Keep the cable free of loops.
configureDetectorTrimAlt: The detector cable passes through the fourth gland from the left. The close-up shows the cut about 10 cm from the inside edge of the enclosure.
configureDetectorConnect: Wire the SENSOR connector using the instructions and examples below. Tighten the terminal screws.
configureValveTrimAlt: The valve cable passes through the first gland from the left. The close-up shows the cut about 10 cm from the inside edge of the enclosure.
relay1ConnectValve: Connect the coil to VOUT and GND on RELAY1 according to the manufacturer’s wiring diagram. If polarity is marked, connect the positive lead to VOUT and the negative lead to GND. Tighten the terminal screws.
configureValveGlandAlt: Outside view of the enclosure with gland 1 highlighted.
configureValveGland: Feed the solenoid valve cable through the first gland from the left when facing the gland panel from outside the enclosure.
configureTerminalAdjustCable: Loosen the cable gland nut and gently pull the excess cable out of the enclosure. Leave a gentle curve inside, with no loops or tension at the connector. Tighten the nut around the outer cable jacket.
configureTerminalAdjustCableAlt: The cable curves gently between the connector and the gland. An arrow outside the enclosure shows which way to pull the excess cable.
configureTerminalPrepSafety: Prepare the wires with power disconnected.
configureTerminalTrimAlt: The Autolejek circuit board is shown inside the open enclosure. A close-up shows side cutters trimming the cable about 10 cm from the inside edge of the enclosure next to the gland.
configureTerminalTrim: Trim the excess with side cutters. Leave about 10 cm of cable inside the enclosure, measured from the inside edge next to the gland. Check that the conductors reach the terminals without tension. Avoid coiling the cable, as a coiled signal cable can pick up interference and cause incorrect pulse counts.
configureTerminalStripAlt: The exposed conductor after sliding off the cut insulation.
configureTerminalFerrules: We recommend fitting ferrules to stranded conductors. Match the ferrule to the conductor size and terminal, then crimp it with a ferrule crimper.
configureTerminalUnplug: Grip the plastic connector housing and pull it straight out of its socket.
configureTerminalBlockAlt: Autolejek circuit board with a rectangular outline around connector 3 for the water meter.
configureTerminalInsertWires: Loosen the terminal screws. Insert each conductor into the correct terminal according to the component wiring diagram, then tighten the screws.
configureTerminalRefit: Refit the connector in its socket.
configureGlandsTitle: Route the cable through the PG9 gland
configureWaterMeterGland: Feed the water meter cable through the third gland from the left when facing the gland panel from outside the enclosure.
configureWaterMeterGlandAlt: The outside view of the enclosure highlights gland 3 for the water meter cable.
configureGlandsNut: Hold the gland body and unscrew the outer compression nut.
configureGlandsCable: Pass the cable through the nut, then through the gland body, from outside into the enclosure.
configureMountDrawing: Drawing of the 151.13 × 135.99 × 50.00 mm enclosure with four M5 mounting holes spaced 80 × 140 mm centre to centre
configureDisconnectSafety: Before you begin, make sure no voltage is applied to the controller or its terminals. Do not touch the circuit board or any electronic components under any circumstances.
configureFrontScrews: Facing the front panel, unscrew the four outer screws A–D.
configureFrontAlt: Front view showing the four outer screws marked A–D
configureCloseFrontText: Keep the power disconnected after wiring the external devices. If you unplugged the keypad or display, reconnect their cables to the respective connectors.
configureDisplayConnectorWarning: The display plug fits in only one orientation. Match the shape of the plug to the socket and slide it straight in without forcing it. If you feel resistance, pull it back and check its alignment.
configureCloseFrontScrews: Refit the front panel, make sure the cables are clear of its edges, and tighten the four screws A–D.
configureFrontCables: Gently move the front panel aside and support it so the cables stay slack. We recommend keeping the keypad and display connected. If the panel makes it hard to reach the external device connectors, you can unplug both cables with the power disconnected. Hold the plugs and gently pull them out. Put the screws somewhere safe.
configureLead: Here you will find the information needed to start and correctly configure Autolejek for your own installation.
relay1VoltageRule: When RELAY1 is energised, its connector supplies the same voltage as the Autolejek power input.
relay1CompatibilityTitle: Match the device to the supply
relay1CompatibilityText: Match the coil voltage to the Autolejek supply voltage. Check the rated output current and power before connecting the valve.
relay1PolarityWarning: Connect wires only while power is switched off. Check the terminal markings on the specific coil before startup. Correct polarity is especially important when the coil or plug contains a diode or another protection circuit.
detectorWiringTitle: How do you connect a detector to Autolejek?
detectorWiringIntro: The Autolejek detector connector has three terminals: 5V, SENSOR, and GND. Their use depends on the output type of the sensor.
detectorWiringConnectorAlt: Lower edge of the Autolejek board. A red frame highlights detector connector 4 with GND, SENSOR and 5V terminals.
detectorWiringConnectorCaption: The SENSOR detector connector on the Autolejek board.
detectorWiringMiddlePin: The middle pin, labelled SENSOR on the board, is the detector signal input.
detectorWiringCurrentLimit: A detector powered from the 5V terminal must not draw more than 200 mA. This is the maximum current available from the connector's power output, not the signal current.
detectorWiring5vConnection: Sensor supply wire, only when the device requires and supports 5 V
detectorWiringGndConnection: Sensor ground wire or the second wire of a volt-free contact
detectorWiringPassiveText: If the detector is an ordinary volt-free contact, such as a float switch or limit switch, connect one wire to SENSOR and the other to GND. Leave the 5V terminal unconnected. The SENSOR input has its own 2.2 kΩ pull-up resistor to 5 V inside Autolejek, and closing the contact to GND changes the input state.
detectorPassiveImageAlt: Passive liquid-level sensor connected to the Autolejek SENSOR and GND terminals
detectorPassiveImageCaption: Example of a passive float-type liquid-level sensor.
detectorFloatCompatibilityWarning: Every level detector must be suitable for the liquid being detected, the tank material, and the installation's operating conditions. Not every sensor can be used with drinking water, fuel, oil, fertiliser, corrosive substances, or high-temperature liquids. Before installation, confirm with the manufacturer that the sensor, cable, and seal materials, measurement method, and mounting arrangement are compatible with the liquid, its temperature and pressure, and the tank wall.
detectorWiringPassiveRule: Connect a passive contact between SENSOR and GND. Do not apply an external voltage to such a contact.
detectorCmwText: The CMW115 is a passive magnetic float sensor with a reed contact. Movement of the float as the liquid level changes opens or closes the contact. The sensor is 118 mm long and 17 mm in diameter, with a cable approximately 0.5 m long. The seller states maximum contact ratings of 0.1 A and 50 V DC; the Autolejek input places a much smaller load on it.
detectorCmwSensorWire: Connect either of the sensor's two wires to the SENSOR input.
detectorCmwGndWire: Connect the other sensor wire to GND. The reed contact has no polarity, so swapping these two wires does not affect operation.
detectorCmwFiveVolt: Leave this terminal unconnected—the passive reed contact does not require a separate power supply.
detectorCmwModeText: Before selecting the signal mode, test the sensor with a multimeter in both float positions. If the alarm condition closes SENSOR to GND, the voltage changes from 5 V to 0 V—select the falling signal. If the condition opens the contact and the voltage changes from 0 V to 5 V—select the rising signal. Always perform a controlled shutdown test after installation.
detectorCmwLink: View the CMW115 magnetic liquid-level sensor.
detectorWiringActiveText: For a typical three-wire sensor, connect its supply wire to 5V, ground to GND, and signal output to SENSOR. Before wiring, verify in the documentation that the sensor supports a 5 V supply, its output is compatible with 5 V logic, and its current consumption does not exceed 200 mA. An open-collector output requires the sensor ground and Autolejek GND to be common.
detectorDfrobotText: The DFRobot SEN0204 is a digital non-contact liquid level sensor. It can be installed on the outside of a suitable tank, so it does not contact the liquid. The manufacturer specifies a 5–24 V supply, 5 mA current consumption, a 500 ms response time, and detection through a tank wall up to 13 mm thick.
detectorDfrobotImageAlt: Non-contact liquid-level sensor installed on the outside of a tank
detectorDfrobotImageCaption: Example of non-contact liquid-level monitoring through a tank wall.
detectorDfrobotVcc: Connect the sensor supply wire to the Autolejek 5V terminal.
detectorDfrobotOut: Connect the sensor's digital signal output to the middle SENSOR terminal.
detectorDfrobotGnd: Connect the sensor ground to the Autolejek GND terminal.
detectorDfrobotFiveVoltRule: When using this sensor with Autolejek, power it only with 5 V. According to the manufacturer, the OUT high-state voltage equals the supply voltage. Powering the sensor with 12 V or 24 V would apply the same voltage to the SENSOR input and could damage the controller.
detectorDfrobotLogicText: When the SEN0204 detects liquid, its OUT pin changes to the high state—approximately 5 V with the recommended Autolejek connection. When the sensor no longer detects liquid, its output changes to the low state, approximately 0 V.
detectorDfrobotLowLevelText: When the sensor is installed near the bottom of the tank, loss of liquid changes the signal from 5 V to 0 V. Set the Autolejek detector signal mode to falling. The alarm activates when the sensor stops detecting liquid.
detectorDfrobotHighLevelText: When the sensor is installed near the top of the tank, liquid reaching the sensor changes the signal from 0 V to 5 V. Set the Autolejek detector signal mode to rising. The alarm activates when liquid is detected at this height.
detectorDfrobotLink: View the DFRobot SEN0204 sensor and its documentation.
detectorWiringWarning: The voltage at the SENSOR input must not exceed 5 V. Do not connect a 12 V or 24 V signal to it. After wiring, configure the detector's active state and verify its operation in a controlled test.
firstSetupIntro: During initial startup, configure at least the calibration, flow meter, maximum tank capacity, and active relay. Without these parameters, the controller cannot count liquid correctly, enforce the permitted filling limit, or activate the correct output. Observe the actual liquid flow during a test fill and use it to select the minimum-flow limit. For example, if normal flow is approximately 23 L/min, the minimum flow can be set to 15 L/min.
firstSetupStep1: Set the interface language in Settings > Language as described in section 6.1, Language.
firstSetupStep2: Set flow-meter calibration in Settings > Calibration as described in section 6.2, Calibration.
firstSetupStep3: Set the maximum tank capacity in Settings > Liquid limit as described in section 6.3, Liquid limit.
firstSetupStep4: Check the flow-meter signal mode as described in section 6.4.1, Signal edge.
firstSetupStep5: Select the active relay or both relays as described in section 6.5, Relays.
firstSetupStep6: If you use an additional sensor, enable and configure the Detector as described in section 6.6, Detector.
firstSetupStep7: Observe the current liquid flow during a test fill. Then configure the minimum-flow alarm in the Flow menu as described in section 6.7.1, Minimum flow, selecting a limit below the normal flow.
firstSetupStep8: To protect the flow meter against excessive flow, enable the maximum-flow alarm in the Flow menu as described in section 6.7.2, Maximum flow, and set its limit.
firstSetupStep9: Return to the main screen, enter a small test limit, and perform a test.
firstSetupManualLink: Open chapter 9 of the user manual
firstSetupPrecheck: Before switching on the power, compare the equipment, connections, protection and cables with the installation wiring diagram. Define the supply voltage and capacity, cable types, lengths and routing, and required shielding and ground/PE connections. Record these details in the project documentation.
firstSetupSwitching: During a controlled trial, check counting, the detector and relays while starting the pump and switching the valve. Check that no pulses are counted without flow and verify behaviour after switching the power off and back on.
firstSetupRecord: Record equipment models, hardware and firmware versions, settings and trial results. Resolve false pulses, resets or unintended switching before normal operation; increasing the filter time alone does not complete the diagnosis.
firstSetupChanges: Discuss changes to the power supply, cables, enclosure, pump, valves and firmware with the person responsible for the installation. Update the documentation and determine which checks must be repeated.
configureMountText: The base has four mounting holes for M5 screws, with 80 × 140 mm centre-to-centre spacing. Install the controller in a dry location protected from rain and direct sunlight. Keep the keypad, display, switch and cables accessible. Avoid dusty locations. Install and store the controller at temperatures from 0°C to 40°C.
configureRelayLedsText: LED1 corresponds to relay P1 and LED2 to relay P2. An illuminated indicator means that relay is energized.
configureRelayLedsAlt: Controller relay indicators LED1 and LED2
configureComLedsText: LED3 indicates failed communication with the display during the startup test; LED4 indicates failed communication with the keypad controller. If an indicator stays on after startup, disconnect power and check the relevant module connection. These indicators do not monitor communication during normal operation.
configureComLedsAlt: Communication diagnostic indicators LED3 and LED4
configureFuseText: Disconnect power to the controller and switched circuit. Check the load, cables, insulation and terminals. Do not fit a fuse with a higher current rating. Replace it after resolving the cause; if the cause is unclear, have a qualified person diagnose the installation.
configureFalsePulsesText: Do not start normal filling. Check the GND connection and signal cable routing relative to pump and relay wiring. Set filtering according to the sensor documentation and check whether the cable needs shortening or shielding.
configureManualDetails: Full troubleshooting in chapter 10 of the Polish manual
configureOperatorCheck: Before filling, prepare a quick stopping method: A or B on the filling screen and disconnecting power to the actuator circuit. Alarms and the detector do not replace operator supervision.
